PWA 1480 is a modern single crystal nickel-base superalloy used in advanced aircraft gas turbines and being considered for the Space Shuttle Main Engine.
The alloy has a microstructure consisting of 55-60% volume fraction of cuboidal γ' precipitates with an average size of 0.5 μm dispersed in a γ matrix.
The yield strength of PWA 1480 is constant at around 1100 MPa from 20-760°C, above which it drops rapidly and becomes strain rate dependent.
Deformation at low temperatures (below 760°C) is dominated by shearing of the γ' precipitates by pairs of a/2<110> dislocations on {111} planes.
At high temperatures (above 815-927°C depending on strain rate), deformation is dominated by γ' by-pass mechanisms.
The true activation energy for yielding is zero at low temperatures, but increases to 500 kJ/mol at high temperatures, indicative of a diffusion-controlled process.
The deformation substructures evolve from planar slip and γ' shearing at low temperatures to more homogeneous and non-planar structures at high temperatures.
Existing precipitation hardening models cannot adequately describe the low temperature yielding behavior of PWA 1480 due to the observation that precipitate penetration is not the rate-limiting step.
The Brown-Ham by-pass model provides a reasonable fit to the high temperature yielding data, but does not account for the effects of thermal activation.
The three distinct temperature regimes observed indicate a fundamental relationship between the deformation mechanisms and activation energies for yielding in this alloy.

The deformation mechanisms observed at the yield point can differ from those inferred from specimens tested to failure, highlighting the importance of characterizing the initial deformation substructures.
This work provides critical data and insights to support the development of physically-based constitutive models for PWA 1480 and similar high volume fraction γ/γ' superalloys.
Single crystal superalloys like PWA 1480 exhibit superior creep, oxidation, and fatigue resistance compared to conventionally cast alloys due to the lack of grain boundaries.
The alloy composition of PWA 1480 includes Ni, Cr, Co, Al, Ti, Ta, W, and Mo, with Al and Ti being the primary γ' formers.
The heat treatment of PWA 1480 consists of solutionizing at 1285°C, followed by two-step aging at 1080°C and 870°C.
